entities.summary:
José Antonio Manso de Velasco y Sánchez de Samaniego, 1st Count of Superunda, was a Spanish military officer and politician who served as the governor of Chile and viceroy of Peru from 1726 to 1747.

As governor of Chile, Manso de Velasco oversaw the construction of numerous roads, bridges, and public buildings, significantly improving the infrastructure of the region.

His tenure as viceroy of Peru was marked by attempts to address the economic and social problems faced by the indigenous population, including the implementation of reforms to reduce the exploitation of the native workforce.

Manso de Velasco's legacy extends beyond his administrative roles, as he was also a patron of the arts, supporting the work of several prominent artists and writers.



In 1767, Manso de Velasco died on January 5th, at the age of 78, leaving behind a lasting impact on the development of Chile and Peru.
